headline: Lower oil prices trim profit; debt milestone reached
summary_short: Occidental's Q3 2026 EPS was $1.61 (adjusted $1.91 from continuing operations) on production of 1,427 Mboed, above the guidance midpoint; principal debt fell to $10.0 billion.
summary_long: Oil and gas pre-tax income was $2.6 billion versus $2.8 billion in Q2, with lower realized crude prices partly offset by higher domestic gas prices. Realized crude fell 11% to $85.91 per barrel. Midstream and marketing pre-tax income dropped to $55 million from $1.3 billion on narrower Waha-to-Gulf-Coast spreads and crude sale timing. Operating cash flow was $4.1 billion and free cash flow before working capital $2.8 billion.
confidence_notes: Revenue, operating income and net income are Yahoo-sourced shard values; EPS and debt are SEC XBRL. Adjusted EPS and cash-flow figures are from the release. No numeric forward guidance was captured beyond the statement of exceeding the production midpoint.

drivers.explanation: Oil and gas decrease was primarily driven by lower realized crude oil prices, partially offset by higher domestic natural gas prices.

Midstream and marketing income fell on lower gas margins from narrower Waha-to-Gulf-Coast spreads and lower crude margins from sale timing, partly offset by higher sulfur volumes and prices at Al Hosn.
The gap between reported and adjusted income mainly reflects derivatives losses.
Management cut principal debt by $1.8 billion in the quarter to $10.0 billion and is pursuing over $4.0 billion of added annual sustainable cash flow by 2030.
